findings: block_score EXPOSURE FIX VALIDATED. Controlled experiment on modern/exterior_daylight/run-w3nextgen-t0007.jpg (2560x1440), one encoder, q=95 constant, only luminance varied: raw block_score 1.031 (L=105.1) -> 1.101 (L=52.3) -> 1.192 (L=31.1) -> 1.308 (L=18.4). The excess above 1 is very nearly inversely proportional to mean luminance ((bs-1)*L = 3.2, 5.3, 6.0, 5.7). Therefore block_score_rel = 1 + (block_score - 1) * (mean_luminance / 128) removes the confound: same four treatments give 1.025, 1.041, 1.047, 1.044 -- spread 0.019 vs 0.277, a ~15x reduction. Lossless PNG control at the same four exposures gives rel 0.989/0.997/0.999/1.000, so the null is exposure-independent. Quality sweep still discriminates: bright q95/85/70/50/30 -> rel 1.025/1.144/1.291/1.456/1.706; dark(x0.18) -> 1.044/1.118/1.222/1.340/1.578. L_ref=128 is mid-grey of the 8-bit range, chosen as a principled anchor not a fit.
